chunks: Abu al-Faraj Muhammad ibn al-Mudaffar ibn Nafees al-Masri, the jurist, told us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Dawudi told us, from his father, saying: I was at the place of Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh, may Allah sanctify his soul,

a man asked him about the meaning of Abbas's statement to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'Indeed, your paternal uncle Abu Talib has accepted Islam by the calculation of the camel' - and he counted thirty-six with his hand. So he said: By that he meant 'Ilah Ahad Jawad', and the interpretation of that is that the Alif is one, the Laam is thirty, the Haa is five, the Alif is one and the Hhaa is eight, the Daal is four, the Jeem is three, the Waw is six, the Alif is one, and the Daal is four. Hence, that is thirty-six.

key_terms.أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ رُوحٍ: Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh, a prominent Shia scholar
key_terms.أَبُو طَالِبٍ: Abu Talib, paternal uncle of the Prophet
key_terms.إِلَهُ أَحَدٍ جَوَادٍ: One God, Generous (phrase used for calculation)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'calculation of the camel' in relation to Abu Talib's Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* elucidates the esoteric meaning of 'hisab al-jamal' (calculation of the camel) as a reference to the phrase 'Ilah Ahad Jawad' (One God, Generous) using Abjad numerals. The sum of thirty-six corresponds to the number of fingers or knots Abu Talib used to signify his silent acceptance of Islam, a detail corroborated by the Prophet’s gesture. This interpretation highlights the Shia scholarly tradition of finding hidden numerical and linguistic signs in the Prophet’s family’s actions.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	We were told by Abu’l-Faraj, Muhammed bin Mudaffar bin Nafees al-Masri, the jurist, that he said: Were told by Abu’l-Hasan, Muhammed bin Ahmad al-Dawudi, from his father, that he said: I was at the place of Abu’l-Qasem, Hussain bin Ruh, may Allah sanctify his soul,

and a man asked him about the meaning of Abbas to the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family: «Indeed, your paternal uncle, Abu Talib, has accepted Islam by the calculation of the camel» and he counted thirty-six with his hand. So he said: By that he meant: «One God» , and the interpretation of that is that the Alif is one, the Laam is thirty, the Haa’ is five, the Alif is one, the Hhaa’ is eight, the Daal is four, the Jeem is three, the Waw is six, the Alif is one and the Daal is four. Hence, that is thirty-six.
